name: Child’s Pose
hero_alt: Child’s Pose, seen from the side
meta_description: Hips hovering above your heels, neck holding your head up, arms working to reach? Two things usually keep Child’s Pose from feeling restful, and a gentle fix for each.
og_description: Two things usually keep Child’s Pose from feeling restful, and a gentle daily exercise for each.
lede: Hips sinking toward your heels, arms long, forehead down and neck soft. Here’s the rubric Posewise measures it against, and what to train when you miss.
rubric_intro: Posewise checks four things from the side. Here’s what good looks like.

rubric.name: Arms
rubric.good: Long and relaxed in front of you

fixes.outcome: your arms will rest long without strain.
fixes.why: Tight lats and shoulders can make a long forward reach feel like work. In a resting pose, it shouldn’t.
fixes.cue: Walk your fingertips forward, then let your arms go heavy.

fixes.outcome: your head will rest heavy on the mat.
fixes.why: The neck is usually the last thing to let go. Slow breathing helps it soften.
fixes.cue: Let your forehead rest down and your neck go completely soft.

cues: And two cues: let your hips settle back toward your heels (widen your knees or slide a cushion under your hips if they don’t reach), and let your arms rest long and relaxed in front of you.

faq.q: Should my hips touch my heels in Child’s Pose?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Let them sink as far as is comfortable; widen your knees or put a folded blanket between your hips and heels.

faq.q: What if my forehead doesn’t reach the floor in Child’s Pose?
faq.a: Rest it on a block, a cushion or your stacked fists. The point is to let your head be supported.

faq.q: Should my knees be together or apart in Child’s Pose?
faq.a: Either. Knees wide gives your belly and hips room to sink; knees together rounds your back more. Pick whichever feels more restful.

faq.q: Where should my arms go in Child’s Pose?
faq.a: Forward for a gentle shoulder stretch, or back alongside your body, palms up, to let your shoulders rest. Both are correct.

faq.q: How can I check my Child’s Pose form at home?
faq.a: Film yourself from the side. Or use Posewise, an iPhone app that measures your Child’s Pose with the camera, speaks corrections as you hold it, and builds a six-minute daily plan for what it finds.

llms_summary: the two things that usually keep Child’s Pose from feeling restful (tight lats and shoulders making the forward reach work, and a neck that won’t let go), with the alignment rubric and a gentle daily exercise for each.
